task_description_correction_carried_forw: RuleApply = RuleApplySt Unit is NOT a definitional equality and must not be attempted. RuleApplySt Atom Unit has an extra `Unit ->` argument and an extra `x Unit` result component; neither `Unit -> X = X` nor `X x Unit = X` holds definitionally, and forcing it would require editing RuleApply, which the purely-additive constraint forbids. The relationship is an explicit liftRuleApply embedding plus three proved bridges. Plan Phase 2 requires docstrings to say `bridged`, never `definitional`.
implementer_pitfalls_carried_forward: The fuel = 0 case of modalExpandBranchesGen_eq_St is `simp only [modalExpandBranchesGen, modalExpandBranchesGenSt]` ONLY when the declarations live inside Saturation.lean (Lean shares the auxiliary matcher within a module). In a separate module the same simp only leaves an apparently-reflexive `X = X` goal that rfl refuses, and an explicit `cases hf : (branches.zip accs).findSome? ...` is needed. Paste artifacts/st-ladder-verified.lean directly into Saturation.lean; do NOT develop in a scratch module. artifacts/st_probe.lean is the separate-module variant and is NOT what lands.

Do not prove modalStepBranchGen_eq_St by induction on the branch b: `apply sf b acc` closes over the whole branch, not the tail, so the IH is about the wrong function. Factor Option.map out of findSome? first via findSome?_map_comm.

Do not reformulate the state list as List.replicate accs.length (). The `accs.map fun _ => ()` form is what makes the induction close with no side hypothesis, because it commutes through the loop's ++ appends and List.replicate.
Do not use StateM/StateT. The subsystem is deliberately monad-free and computable; a monadic formulation would change the elaborated term shape every downstream unfold depends on.
Anchor every edit on declaration names, never line numbers.
